report.source_text: Native T1-mapping demonstrated markedly elevated T1 values with preponderance in the inferoseptal wall (1068 ± 73 ms in the entire slice vs. 1122 ± 31 ms in the inferoseptal wall), also see Figs. 1a and 2a. Furthermore, T2-mapping revealed increased values (entire slice 52 ± 6 ms, inferoseptal wall 55 ± 6 ms), suggesting myocardial edema representing active myocardial inflammation by hantavirus infection. In contrast, the LGE image, potentially indicating irreversible myocardial damage if positive, in the corresponding slice was negative (Fig. 1c).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 36-year-old male presented to the emergency department with headache and abdominal pain. Initial laboratory and serological workup confirmed Puumala virus infection (IgG/IgM antibodies positive by ELISA and immunoassay). Concurrent findings included thrombocytopenia (71,000/μl), acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.0-3.0 mg/dl), massive proteinuria, and elevated CRP (8.6 mg/dl). ECG showed sinus bradycardia (40/min), T-wave inversion in lead V2, and incomplete right bundle branch block. At 6 days post-admission, cardiac biomarkers were elevated (troponin I 0.32 μg/l, CK 319 U/l). Cardiac MRI demonstrated markedly elevated native T1-mapping values (1122 ± 31 ms in inferoseptal wall) and increased T2-mapping values (55 ± 6 ms in inferoseptal wall) consistent with myocardial edema and active inflammation, with negative late gadolinium enhancement. Coronary artery disease was excluded by coronary CT angiography. Echocardiography showed normal left ventricular function (65%) without regional wall motion abnormalities. The patient was admitted to the nephrology department for supportive therapy and showed rapid clinical improvement over the following weeks with resolution of chest pain and dyspnea.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Confirmed Puumala virus infection as the causative agent
Elevated cardiac biomarkers indicating myocardial injury
CMR findings of active myocardial inflammation with conspicuous native T1 and T2 mapping abnormalities
Normal cardiac function on echocardiography despite myocardial inflammation

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Coronary CT angiography excluded coronary artery disease; normal echocardiography without regional wall motion abnormalities; elevated troponin explained by myocarditis rather than atherosclerotic plaque rupture

Negative late gadolinium enhancement on CMR indicates absence of irreversible myocardial damage; elevated T1 and T2 mapping values indicate reversible myocardial edema consistent with active inflammation rather than chronic fibrosis

Confirmed Puumala virus serology (IgG/IgM) with clinical and imaging findings consistent with viral myocarditis; systemic manifestations (thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, proteinuria) typical of hantavirus infection

remaining_uncertainties: Specific timing of symptom onset relative to viral exposure (incubation period not documented)
Details of supportive therapy provided during hospitalization
Long-term cardiac follow-up and repeat imaging to document complete resolution of myocardial inflammation
Whether patient had any hemodynamic compromise or arrhythmias during hospitalization despite normal ejection fraction
